_note: Thuso Money's vouchers, Wave 4 of the approved build plan: a prepaid amount towards a visit or a MyThuso for Mom plan, issued over the counter by a corner shop or by the back office, and redeemed by whoever holds its code against something they owe. packages/engines/src/money/domain/vouchers.ts holds the arithmetic, the web preview's checkout runs the same code, and every refusal sentence a route answers with is packages/catalog/apis/money.json's, found by route and id. Nothing here is a real service: no voucher is sold, no shop is contracted, no value is held for anybody and no code opens anything.
_whyNoNativeEmitter: Neither native app redeems a voucher in this wave. A code is typed at the web preview's checkout and nowhere else, so a generated Swift and Kotlin copy of this file would be a copy nobody renders, and a copy nobody renders is the one that drifts. The day a phone takes a voucher, scripts/emit-vouchers.mjs is written with the screen that reads it.

towards.why: A voucher towards a visit is issued at the catalogue's price for that visit on the day it is issued, and pays towards any visit a person owes for. The amount is never typed by the shop or the desk: a voucher for an amount somebody chose is a gift card for anything, and the catalogue is where a price is.
A voucher towards MyThuso for Mom is issued at one tier's monthly price and pays towards a plan's month, which is how a family member far away puts a month of a parent's plan into somebody's hand.

towardsWhy: A voucher towards a visit pays for visits and one towards a plan pays for plans, and neither pays for the other. The line keeps a voucher sold as a month of a parent's plan from being spent by somebody else on something the buyer never meant, and it keeps the arithmetic of both payables the catalogue's.
neverTowardsWhy: Section 18A of the Medicines and Related Substances Act 101 of 1965 prohibits supplying a medicine under a bonus, rebate or incentive scheme, and the founder's decision in the approved build plan refuses any reward for taking a medicine pending counsel (packages/catalog/medicines.json adherence). A voucher tied to a medicine — towards buying one, collecting a script, or earned by taking a dose — is that scheme with a code on it. So a voucher is issued only towards a visit or a plan, a request naming any of these words as what it is towards or as a field it carries is refused in its own sentence, and a voucher is never redeemed against anything but a visit or a plan payable. A plan that includes collecting medicine may be paid for with a voucher, because the plan is paid for, not the medicine.

cashOut.whatIsLeft: What is left on a voucher stays on it until it expires. It is never paid out, moved to a wallet or a bank, or added to.
cashOut.why: A voucher that can become cash is a way to move money that nobody is billing for, and a prepaid amount MyThuso would be holding like a bank. So a voucher is issued only towards a visit or a plan, redeemed only against a payable, and a request that asks for a cash, wallet, bank or airtime outcome — by what it is towards or by a field it sends — is refused rather than ignored. A cancelled visit's redemption goes back onto the voucher, never to a card or a hand.

expiry.keptOnIssue: A voucher keeps the expiry in force on the day it was issued. A later change reaches vouchers issued after it, and never one already in somebody's hand.

law.subject: Prepaid certificates, credits and vouchers
law.reading: A prepaid certificate, credit, voucher or similar device stays valid until it is fully redeemed, and for at least three years after it was issued.
law.needsCounsel: Counsel has not confirmed that section 63 reaches a voucher towards a health visit or a plan, what happens to an amount left on a voucher when it expires, or whether a voucher issued free by the back office is a prepaid certificate at all. Until counsel does, the shortest expiry an admin may set is three years for every voucher, which is the reading that protects the person holding one.
law.proposedBecause: The founder instructed that the expiry be an admin setting whose lower bound is three years, from section 63. The bound is read from here by packages/catalog/money.json's setting and scripts/check-boundaries.mjs holds the two to each other, so the three years live in one place.

expiry.afterExpiry: An expired voucher cannot be redeemed, and what was left on it is not paid out. What becomes of that amount is a question for counsel, and it is not answered here.

length.proposedBecause: Twelve characters from an alphabet of thirty-two, read aloud at a till or typed on a phone, in three groups of four. Thirty-two to the twelfth is more than a million million million codes, so guessing one is not a strategy and no attempt limit is needed; a six-digit code, like the cash code, would need one.

codes.alphabetWhy: No O and 0, no I and 1, because a code misread at a counter is a code refused at a door.
codes.kept: Money keeps a salted digest of a voucher's code and never the code. The code is shown once, in the answer to whoever issued it, and the runtime keeps it out of its replay table.
codes.why: A voucher's code is a bearer credential: whoever holds it spends it. So it is random, derived from nothing a person can see, shown once, kept as a digest, and carried in a request body rather than a path, where a server's log would keep it.

redemption.why: A voucher pays as much of what is owed as it holds and no more, and what is owed afterwards is paid in the ordinary way through POST /v1/money/payments@2. A voucher that covers the whole of a payable settles it, and a payment for a payable already settled is refused as already paid.
redemption.cancelled: When a visit a voucher paid towards is cancelled, the amount goes back onto the voucher with the expiry it already had. It is never refunded to a card, because it never came from one.

preview.why: The web checkout has nobody who sold the reader a voucher, so a simulated corner shop issues one in the tab's memory when somebody asks to use a voucher, and the screen says so beside the code. It is towards the visit the Mom Essential plan includes, at that visit's price.

screen.heading: Use a voucher
screen.intro: A voucher pays towards a visit from the catalogue. What it does not cover is paid in the ordinary way.
screen.issuedInPreview: A simulated corner shop issued this voucher in this tab, because nobody sold you one: {code}. It is towards a {service}, and it expires on {expires}.
screen.redeemed: {amount} of the voucher paid towards this visit. {left} stays on it until {expires}.
screen.covered: The voucher covers this visit. Nothing else is owed.
screen.never: A voucher is never paid out in cash, and never tied to a medicine.
